strengths: Novel dual-memory architecture with well-motivated design: gated global memory for long-range dependencies and FIFO temporary memory for recent context effectively address limitations of prior finite-state models

Remarkable empirical results: achieves 100% accuracy retrieving passkeys across all positions in 1M-token sequences despite training only on 32k contexts; matches fine-tuned full-attention performance on SCROLLS summarization tasks
Comprehensive experimental validation spanning academic benchmarks (SCROLLS with 7 diverse tasks), synthetic tasks (passkey), and real-world applications (user behavior QA, agent tasks)

Significant practical efficiency: maintains constant ~10GB memory footprint and stable ~22ms decode latency regardless of context length; achieves 21× speedup and 10× memory reduction versus full attention at 1M tokens
Valuable methodological contribution: layer-level pipeline parallelism yields 2.7× training speedup over naive context parallelism, enabling 128k context fine-tuning on 16×80GB GPUs
Practical plug-and-play integration into pre-trained models with minimal fine-tuning (3 epochs on 32k contexts); parameter-efficient design using low-rank adapters
Strong ablation studies (Figure 8) clearly demonstrating distinct roles of global versus temporary memory components, with gating visualization providing interpretability (Figures 10-11)
Clear presentation with well-designed architectural diagrams, comprehensive experimental tables, and detailed efficiency analysis comparing prefill/decode phases
weaknesses: Complexity claims overstated: terminology 'constant memory usage' misleading—method uses bounded fixed-size memory (~2.5k tokens), which is better than linear but not asymptotically constant; no formal proofs or rigorous complexity analysis provided; missing approximation error analysis
Limited model scale: experiments exclusively on Qwen3-4B; no validation on larger models (13B, 70B+) standard in modern NLP; generalization to different model architectures unexplored
Training scope limitations: fine-tuning only on 32k contexts; sensitivity to different training lengths unexplored; unclear how performance scales with variable training sequence lengths

Statistical rigor gaps: no confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars reported; some SCROLLS differences appear within noise margins (e.g., 62.5 vs 61.0); Table 7 shows memory sensitivity but boundary conditions not explored

Reproducibility concerns: proprietary datasets (e-commerce UQA, Long-Horizon Agent Dataset) prevent independent validation; code link not provided; hyperparameter justification sparse (e.g., rank=8 for RLA); domain-specific real-world evaluation

Incomplete baseline coverage: missing recent strong methods (StreamingLLM, advanced positional interpolation approaches); memory budget alignment (~3k tokens) for all methods not rigorously justified; limited comparison with linear attention variants

Passkey task limitations: impressive extrapolation result but synthetic benchmark tests position-bias robustness in isolation rather than comprehensive long-context understanding; 1M extrapolation doesn't necessarily validate semantic understanding at extreme lengths

Technical details underspecified: gradient flow through parallel memory paths in update mechanism unexplained; FIFO queue design not compared against attention-based or learned selection; compression token interleaving strategy not ablated; computational overhead of gating mechanism not analyzed

Real-world evaluation concerns: UQA improvement (78.7 vs 76.0) lacks error bars; agent task evaluated on single recent benchmark (Terminal-Bench) with limited community establishment; results may not generalize beyond tested domains

Missing ablations and analyses: no systematic extrapolation degradation curves (32k→64k/256k); failure mode analysis absent; information retention rates across memory components not quantified; training efficiency (not just inference) incompletely evaluated

strengths: Well-motivated dual-memory architecture addressing clear limitations of prior finite-state models (information forgetting and loss of recent details)
Impressive passkey extrapolation results: trained on 32k contexts, successfully retrieves information from 1M-token sequences
Comprehensive evaluation across diverse settings: academic benchmarks (SCROLLS), real-world applications (UQA, agent tasks), and synthetic tasks
Effective ablation studies (Section 5.1) demonstrating distinct roles of global memory (extrapolation) vs. temporary memory (in-domain performance)
Practical engineering contribution: layer-level pipeline parallelism achieving 2.7× training speedup over naive context parallelism
Parameter-efficient design (RLA module) enables integration into existing pre-trained models with minimal fine-tuning
Clear presentation and effective visualizations (Figures 2-4, 10) make the architecture easy to understand
Interpretability analysis: gating value visualizations provide insights into memory management across layers
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: The main contribution combines existing techniques (gated memory from LSTMs/GRUs, FIFO queues, low-rank adapters). Direct innovation is incremental—particularly regarding HMT (2025), a concurrent work with similar O(N)/O(1) guarantees that is inadequately differentiated

Overstated empirical claims on SCROLLS: CoMeT underperforms Full Attention on QMSum (35.6 vs. 37.4), and improvements on other tasks are marginal (~1-2 points). The abstract's claim of 'comparable' performance is not uniformly supported

Fairness of comparisons compromised: Different baselines use inconsistent memory budgets (CoMeT: 2,560 tokens, HMT: 3,072, Transformer-XL: 5,120 window) despite claiming '~3k budget' equivalence. Different methods may have optimal training configurations at different lengths

Unreproducible real-world evaluations: UQA uses proprietary anonymous dataset with LLM-as-judge evaluation; Agent task only compares CoMeT vs. xRAG (not vs. full attention) with no raw numbers provided for 'competitive' claim

Passkey task shows near-deterministic gating behavior (Figure 10): Gates collapse to 0 at passkey arrival, 1 thereafter—closer to position memorization than sophisticated memory management. Perfect accuracy on synthetic task does not predict modest SCROLLS improvements

Complexity claims require qualification: Abstract claims O(N) time and O(1) space, but prefill phase is O(N) (Figure 9a shows linear latency growth). Only decode achieves O(1) per-token complexity. This critical distinction is buried in results

Insufficient sensitivity analysis and ablations: RLA rank set to r=8 without justification; compression token spacing (every 8 tokens) appears arbitrary with no ablation; no analysis of hyperparameter sensitivity
Missing comparisons to important baselines: InfiniAttention (Munkhdalai et al., 2024) is cited but not benchmarked; recent 2025 compression methods (GMSA, Perception Compressor) are absent
No statistical significance testing or error bars despite SCROLLS differences of 1-2 points, which may be within noise

Limited analysis of what the model learns: Gating visualizations show mostly closed gates (value ≈1) during normal processing; claims about 'differentiated forgetting rates' are speculative with unclear interpretation
Efficiency claims lack important context: 21× speedup applies only to decode latency; comparison is against vanilla (unoptimized) attention, not FlashAttention or other production implementations
Memory constraint not discussed: With only ~2.5k tokens allocated across 10k+ token documents, it is unclear what critical information for complex reasoning is actually preserved in global memory

strengths: Well-motivated dual-memory architecture (gated global + FIFO temporary) elegantly addresses genuine limitations of prior finite-state methods with clear ablations demonstrating necessity of both components

Impressive empirical results across multiple evaluation dimensions: zero-shot extrapolation (32k→1M tokens), competitive SCROLLS performance matching full attention on summarization tasks, and real-world validation on e-commerce QA and agent tasks

Comprehensive experimental evaluation spanning synthetic tasks (passkey retrieval), academic benchmarks (SCROLLS: 7 diverse tasks), and real-world applications, providing multiple angles on effectiveness
Strong efficiency gains with rigorous analysis: constant O(1) memory (10GB), linear time complexity empirically validated, 21× speedup at 1M tokens with detailed prefill/decode breakdowns
Interpretable architecture with gating visualizations across all layers (Figure 11) showing learned differentiated forgetting rates and clear roles of memory components via ablations
Practical engineering contribution via layer-level pipeline parallelism achieving 2.7× speedup, enabling training on 128k contexts with commodity hardware
Good reproducibility: code release promised, clear hyperparameters, public benchmark usage, detailed appendices, and architectural diagrams enable understanding
weaknesses: Limited to small model scale (Qwen3-4B only). Scalability to 7B, 13B, 70B models unclear; different sizes may require different memory budgets and exhibit different long-context behaviors critical for industrial impact

Key experiments rely on proprietary/non-reproducible data: UQA dataset from undisclosed e-commerce source prevents independent verification; Terminal-Bench evaluation poorly described; Full Attention comparison at 128k missing

Lack of formal theoretical justification: claims of O(N) time and O(1) space lack proofs; no information-theoretic analysis of compression trade-offs or approximation bounds; gating motivation not formally justified versus alternatives

Insufficient hyperparameter sensitivity analysis: compression token frequency (every 8 tokens), RLA rank (fixed at 8), gating function (sigmoid), chunk size (2048) appear arbitrary with no ablations exploring alternatives

Generalization beyond training setup unclear: all models fine-tuned on 32k length; extrapolation robustness to other lengths not characterized; SCROLLS contexts vary (2k-19k) but in-distribution performance at different lengths not analyzed

Design choice justification incomplete: memory initialization procedure (G⁰, T⁰) during inference unclear; separate compression vs. readout tokens not compared to alternatives; gradient flow benefits claimed but not empirically validated

Missing rigor in comparisons: no error bars or confidence intervals; unfair budget allocation ('~3k tokens') may disadvantage some baselines; baseline hyperparameter selection process not described; recent efficient methods (RWKV6, Mamba2) barely compared

strengths: Well-motivated practical problem with high relevance to LLM deployment; quadratic complexity and linear KV cache growth are genuine bottlenecks
Novel dual-memory architecture with clear separation of concerns: gated global memory for long-range dependencies, FIFO temporary memory for recent details; design is well-justified
Remarkable extrapolation capability: trained on 32k contexts, accurately retrieves information from 1M tokens with 21× speedup and 10× memory reduction

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple dimensions: academic benchmarks (SCROLLS with 7 tasks, 2WikiMQA, HotpotQA), synthetic tasks (passkey retrieval), real-world applications (UQA, Terminal-Bench)
Strong empirical results: matches or exceeds full attention on summarization tasks; outperforms all evaluated efficient baselines on average SCROLLS score (40.10 vs 38.24 for SWA)
Thorough ablation studies and analysis: memory allocation effects (Figure 7-8), RLA rank sensitivity, hyperparameter exploration, gating value visualization providing interpretability
Layer-level pipeline parallelism is novel and practical contribution enabling 128k training on 16×80GB GPUs with 2.7× speedup over naive context parallelism
Generalization demonstrated across model families and scales (Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-14B, Llama-3.1-8B) with consistent improvements
Parameter-efficient design with only 0.098% overhead; honest treatment of limitations and failure modes in appendix
weaknesses: Inconsistent performance across tasks: notable gaps on Qasper (35.5 vs 40.3 F1) and QALT (56.0 vs 64.2 F1) without full explanation; information aggregation failures indicate architectural limitations on reasoning tasks
Counterintuitive result on Llama-3.1-8B (CoMeT 104.6% of full attention) raises questions about whether improvements reflect method quality or training dynamics; insufficient analysis of this anomaly

Limited theoretical analysis: claimed O(1) space and O(N) time complexity lack formal proofs; no formalization of when/why gating preserves information; comparison with information-theoretic limits is qualitative

Reproducibility concerns: code URL missing despite availability statement; RLA and gate initialization schemes not detailed; training procedures for real-world datasets sparsely described; mixed dataset construction requires external datasets

Fundamental architectural limitation on aggregation: failure case 00da reveals inherent weakness in gathering information from non-contiguous parts; this isn't tunable and limits reasoning capability

Design choices not thoroughly justified: RLA rank=8 chosen despite small performance variation (Table 6); FIFO queue simplicity vs learned replacement policies not compared; compression token interval (every 8 tokens) appears arbitrary
Missing statistical significance testing and error bars; performance differences are sometimes modest, particularly on shorter sequences

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks, model scales, and real-world tasks with detailed ablations and efficiency analysis
Intuitive and well-motivated dual-memory architecture that effectively balances global long-term retention with temporary recent context awareness
Strong empirical results on summarization tasks, matching full attention performance on GovReport/SummScreenFD with only ~2.5k memory tokens
Practical layer-level pipeline parallelism contribution enabling efficient training on 128k contexts
Clear presentation with well-defined notation, informative visualizations, and extensive appendices supporting reproducibility
Demonstrates impressive length extrapolation: 1M-token passkey retrieval when trained only on 32k sequences
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: primarily combines well-established techniques (chunk recurrence, dual queues, gated updates, compression tokens) from prior work; improvements over HMT are marginal
Misleading complexity claims: O(N) prefill phase still requires processing entire context; O(1) space applies only to per-chunk computation; claims need more careful qualification

Substantial performance gaps on detail-sensitive tasks: Qasper shows 88% retention (35.5 vs 40.3 F1); Appendix J reveals systematic failures in detail preservation, granularity, causal reasoning, and information aggregation

Experimental design concerns: unfair fixed memory budget constraint may favor/disfavor certain methods differently; missing evaluations of recent baselines (DeltaNet, Mamba, HGRN) mentioned in related work; suspicious result that CoMeT outperforms full attention on Llama-3.1-8B

Hyperparameter sensitivity undermines practical usability: Table 9 shows 2WikiMQA ranging 64.4-76.6 EM; many interdependent hyperparameters with limited guidance for practitioners on task-specific selection

No theoretical analysis or insights: lacks formal characterization of information preservation/loss; gating visualization (Fig 10) shown but not interpreted; no analysis of compression bottlenecks
Layer-level pipeline parallelism is standard systems engineering rather than novel research; 2.7× speedup, while useful, is incremental

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across SCROLLS, real-world applications, and synthetic tasks with multiple model families and scales
Well-motivated dual-memory architecture that elegantly addresses limitations of prior finite-state models through explicit gating and FIFO mechanisms

Significant practical contributions: plug-and-play design with minimal parameter overhead (0.098%), layer-level pipeline parallelism achieving 2.7x training speedup, and 21x inference speedup at 1M tokens
Thorough ablation studies clearly demonstrating distinct roles of global memory (extrapolation) vs. temporary memory (in-domain performance) with insightful gating visualizations
Sound technical execution with correct complexity analysis, well-designed experiments, and honest analysis of failure modes (Table 10) showing even full attention struggles on some tasks
Strong empirical results maintaining 95-97.6% of full-attention performance on summarization while achieving constant memory and linear time
weaknesses: Significant performance gaps on specific tasks undermine generalization claims: Qasper shows 4.8 F1 point gap (35.5 vs 40.3), and extrapolation on long sequences shows 13.2 vs 20.4 F1—these are explained post-hoc rather than predictively addressed

Extrapolation claims are overstated: the impressive 1M-token passkey retrieval is a narrow fact-extraction task, not general long-context reasoning; real extrapolation (Table 7) shows substantial degradation
Limited novelty in individual components: gating is LSTM-inspired, FIFO queues are standard, low-rank adaptation is established—contribution is primarily in their combination without novel techniques
Insufficient principled analysis of memory allocation: global/temporary memory sizes (512/2048) appear arbitrary with no theoretical justification for the trade-off or how to set these for new tasks

Baseline comparison shows RWKV7 has 3x faster prefill (0.87s vs 2.7s at 32k tokens), which is a significant throughput disadvantage not adequately discussed; RWKV7 uses parallel prefill but CoMeT's compatibility with this is unexplored
Missing code availability URL and reproducibility concerns: proprietary datasets (UQA, Terminal-Bench) and underspecified implementation details limit reproducibility
Hyperparameter choices (rank=8, compression interval=8, chunk size=2048) derived from 'preliminary experiments' without principled justification, though ablations partially address this

Terminology and claims need precision: 'constant memory' should clarify 'with respect to sequence length'; the term 'collaborative' is not well-justified; model-dependent performance gaps (0.1 vs 4.8 F1 on Qasper) suggest unresolved architectural issues
